data.title: Volkswagen's Osnabrück plant to switch from cars to defence

data.title: 'Polarised Brazil': Lula remains a ‘strong candidate’ despite the challenges of incumbency
data.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Andreza Aruska de Souza Santos, Director of King’s Brazil Institute at the School of Global Affairs, King’s College London and Associate Professor in Brazil and Latin American Studies. According to Aruska, Brazil’s approaching elections can be viewed through competing prisms: macroeconomic performance and political confidence are moving on different tracks. While headline indicators may suggest an economy performing relatively well, she argues that many Brazilians experience a much harsher reality shaped by the cost of living and a volatile job market.

data.title: Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger: what we learned from the year’s biggest rockumentary
data.description: Capturing the band’s 2025 global comeback tour, this two-hour film reveals the tense first rehearsal with Liam, Noel being a big softie and the Gallaghers’ politics – just don’t expect any mention of ticket prices It was the reunion that many thought would never happen: Oasis re-forming for a series of sold-out live shows, their first since Noel and Liam Gallagher split acrimoniously in 2009. For those who managed to get tickets last year, the performances were a celebration of one of Britpop’s finest bands and a chance to live through a night of 90s nostalgia. For the millions who missed out, be it due to demand or budgetary restraints, the tour represented a generational Fomo moment. Luckily, the directors Will Lovelace and Dylan Southern were embedded within team Oasis throughout the whole thing, alongside the Peaky Blinders creator, Steven Knight: the result is Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger , a two-hour concert film that hits cinemas around the world this week. Whether you were on the front row at Manchester’s Heaton Park, doing the Poznan in Seoul or stuck at home watching it all online, Don’t Look Back in Anger captures the Oasis Live ’25 Tour for posterity. Here’s what we learned. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘So big and so close’: going on a bear hunt in northern Spain
data.description: Conservationists have helped Cantabrian brown bears claw their way back from the edge of extinction in the beautiful mountains of Asturias – and carefully controlled nature tourism allows visitors to see them Once upon a time, in the woods outside Pola de Somiedo, lived a family of Cantabrian brown bears. The villagers reported sightings of a mother bear who had lost a leg to a hunter’s trap, her two cubs and two adult males, either of which might have been the father. In those days, at the end of the 1980s, they seemed to be the last of their kind in this part of Asturias. Meanwhile, the wider population dropped to about 60 bears across the surrounding Cantabrian mountain range that gave the species its name. They have since clawed their way back from the edge of extinction here in northern Spain, and nature guide Luis Frechilla believes their numbers may now be upwards of 500 again. “They’re still classed as endangered,” he tells me, until the official count hits 1,000. But relative abundance makes them much easier to see today in Somiedo natural park – one of Spain’s first such protected areas, established in 1988. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘This is dangerous’: slime moulds and the bitter debate over the nature of intelligence
data.description: Scientists are battling over whether supposedly simple organisms should be considered ‘intelligent’. The outcome could reshape our understanding of the natural world – and our own place within it Forty years ago, as an undergraduate in Hokkaido, Toshiyuki Nakagaki came upon a lemon-yellow stain in a petri dish. That encounter turned him into a doyen of slime mould research – and fed a storm of biological and philosophical debate about the meanings of life and intelligence that persists to this day. Before, no one would have called a slime mould “intelligent”; the popular adjective, in fact, was “simple”. “A simple mass of protoplasm,” one 1895 description ran; “among the most simple of organisms”, said another. And it was hard to argue otherwise. A slime mould can appear to be just a small cell, capable only of feeding and reproducing. Simple is as simple does. Of that first meeting, Nakagaki said: “I was just impressed with how fast it moved.” Physarum polycephalum , the slime mould species in that petri dish, has a top speed of 1cm an hour. For amoebic organisms, that’s gold-medal standard. At first glance, Physarum seems to spread as irregularly as ink on blotting paper, but in fact it senses its meals of bacteria or other microbes and reaches for them with a long, thin finger of protoplasm – which not only digests its food but then forages further or pulls back into the rest of the mould. It’s impossible to watch a slime mould over many days without sensing some deliberation at play. Continue reading...

data.title: Colin from Accounts final season review – farewell to a blinding ray of TV sunshine
data.description: After season two’s mortifying ending, the charming hit comedy is back for the last time … with sex parties, extreme cringe and a final answer to the central will-they-won’t-they There are cliffhangers, and then there’s whatever happened at the end of Colin from Accounts’ second season. We had, by that point, witnessed protagonists Ashley and Gordon’s unconventional love story evolve from bizarre meet-cute – key stages: boob-flashing, car accident, injured dog – to soulmate-level relationship. But what starts with an exposed nipple can abruptly go tits up. On a heaving dancefloor at Ash’s best friend’s wedding, Gordon – drunk and buoyed up by the DJ dropping Slice of Heaven by Dave Dobbyn (the Oceanian equivalent of Come on Eileen, judging by the euphoric reaction) – decides to ask his girlfriend to marry him. Ash, humiliated by the circumstances, doesn’t respond. Everyone else films it and laughs. Gordon insists the whole thing was a joke and awkwardly boogies on. Then the credits roll. If you had somehow managed to wipe this eye-watering faux pas from your mind’s eye, fear not: the Aussie rom-sitcom returns for its third and final series by replaying the agonising proposal in full. It gets worse. We discover the pair split soon after and haven’t seen each other for three years. In fact, they’ve both since found other (extremely attractive) partners: the kind but dim David and the hyper-capable and efficient Chelsea. As Ash later observes, they’ve “upgraded” – but you know their respective hearts don’t really belong to their nice new beaux. Continue reading...

What is the end goal of all of this? It is to start something that will then snowball. By occupying key roundabouts at 7am, the group caused a 4-mile-long queue of traffic along the A20, closing it in both directions. Perhaps more significantly, a uniformed gathering that brought to mind the black shirts of Oswald Mosley’s British Union of Fascists in the 1930s forcefully grabbed the nation’s attention. data.title: Knightfall review – low-rent gender-flipped Bond knock-off swaps Aston Martins for Minis
data.description: Jeanine Nerissa Sothcott’s no-nonsense spy heads a game cast that includes Ian Ogilvy and Roger Moore’s son Geoffrey, but this austerity actioner lacks tension Proceeding from an old-school title pun – yes, the heroine goes by the name Ros Knight – the latest from resourceful microbudget producer Jonathan Sothcott surely has one optimistic eye on filling the void left by the withdrawal of 007 from public life. Here is the gender-flipped Bond some have been seeking: the adventures of a no-nonsense, tough-talking security operative (Jeanine Nerissa Sothcott) who is tasked with recovering a lethal bioweapon pilfered from a scaled-down Porton Down during the prologue. Everything, in truth, proves a bit reined-in. This austerity actioner spends less on its set pieces than the Broccolis typically did on keeping one Aston Martin refuelled; the Sothcotts’ car of choice, emblematically, is the dinkiest of Minis. In essence, it’s Bond without the attendant glamour, hanging around drizzly marinas and parky-looking country lanes, in dim light that hopefully obscures some of the more obvious budget limitations. What money there is here has wisely been spent on human resources, faces who might still look good on the promotional material: a cameoing Michael Paré as a shady Felix Leiter type, Roger Moore’s son Geoffrey as our gal’s understandably worried-looking lover, Nick Moran giving cut-price Colin Firth as a meddling bureaucrat. The pick of the players is a spry, characterful Ian Ogilvy as Ros’s estranged father, helpfully identifying where the real power lies on a chessboard and generally steadying scenes whenever matters get a bit too threadbare. Continue reading...

data.title: The Castle by Jon Ronson review – bizarre tales of modern masculinity
data.description: A journalist embarks on a wild good chase that might – or might not – be informative about the male condition Recovering from surgery at home in upstate New York in 2023, Jon Ronson awoke to a string of texts from his adult son about a weird evening he just had at a stranger’s castle in Connecticut. Having gone along with a friend who’d been invited to a party there, he arrived to find a few lost-looking young women with the sixtysomething host, Chris Mark, a steel heir filming a reality show about “101 princesses” whose first rule was “Never say no to King Chris”. As a parent, Ronson is worried; as a reporter of more than 30 years on the cranks-and-crooks beat, he’s already on the clock. After trawling online whispers of sinister goings-on at the castle, he decides to pay a visit to Mark, who proudly shows off the stalactites and waterfall in his “cave-themed” bedroom before explaining how he picks up women on dating apps to “adapt” them to life as “princesses”. “The only girls that really work are drug addicts ... they don’t know what’s going on,” he says. Almost touchingly, Mark asks Ronson to sign an NDA, and the book describes Mark flooding his phone with threats when he declines. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s not good to walk through the world feeling like prey’: Thelma & Louise’s writer on turning a movie classic into a musical
data.description: It was her very first film and it won her an Oscar. But can Callie Khouri now make it work on stage with songs? She talks about what made her write it – and how little has changed since ‘I have a world-class case of beginner’s luck,” says Callie Khouri, who won an Oscar for her very first screenplay, Thelma & Louise . She also scored a hit with her first TV series, Nashville , which lasted six seasons. And at 68, she is taking on another first by penning a musical theatre version of Thelma & Louise, hoping her luck hasn’t run out. “I hope that this is not the end of that streak,” she laughs. “That I don’t hit a wall here and slide down it like Wile E Coyote.” Thelma & Louise isn’t an obvious bet for a musical. A story that features an abusive marriage, attempted rape, murder and double suicide doesn’t scream “jazz hands”, and Khouri had turned down offers before. “My agent said, ‘There’s a guy who wants to meet you to talk about doing Thelma as a stage musical,’” says Khouri. “And I just thought, ‘Well, that’s nuts!’” But the iconic 90s film – starring Susan Sarandon and Geena Davis (and a young Brad Pitt) – is an ultimately triumphant piece of cinema: a feminist road movie driven by the power of female friendship, which still captures imaginations. Khouri was eventually convinced. It’s been a decade in the pipeline, but things took off when uber-producer Sonia Friedman came on board, and now it has premiered at London’s Young Vic, starring Rachel Tucker and Amy Lennox. Continue reading...

data.title: The pest I’ll never forget: the cockroaches were everywhere – even on our wine glasses
data.description: In a cheap London flat with no heating, dozens of the insects swarmed, leading to a Valentine’s Day that still makes me break out in a cold sweat I don’t know if cockroaches really could, as we’re often told, survive a nuclear apocalypse, but I can tell you this with certainty: they can definitely survive pest control. “Hopefully that should be a bit better now,” said the friendly exterminator after his first visit to our flat. By the third visit he was speaking more honestly. “The only way to get rid of your cockroaches,” he said, “would be to burn this whole block of flats to the ground.” It was January 2003 when I moved with my girlfriend Helen into our first London flat. It’s fair to say there were red flags we probably should have spotted. It was suspiciously affordable – £140 a week for a place less than a minute’s walk from Finsbury Park tube station? Sure, the place looked pretty skanky, but it was still spacious for a studio flat. We put the price down to the fact there was absolutely no way of heating the property and signed up. data.title: The byelection here in Holborn and St Pancras is Labour’s to lose. But lose it might | Polly Toynbee
data.description: The Greens appeal to young and progressive voters here on defence, rent controls and North Sea oil. The Burnham bounce may be about to hit an obstacle You might think a byelection showdown between two progressive parties is unimportant when the deep struggle for the national heart is between the right bloc and the left – but the result in Holborn and St Pancras matters. It matters for Andy Burnham and Labour because this is a test of the Burnham bounce: he saw off the right in Makerfield – can he win over the left too? Can he show he has enthusiastic approval from voters in southern constituencies as well as those in the north? For the Greens it matters almost existentially because failing here could send them and their leader, Zack Polanski, back to the political fringes. Holborn and St Pancras, neighbouring Westminster, was vacated (vengefully) by Keir Starmer last week. This plum forever-Labour constituency has attracted 96 Labour applications for selection day on Wednesday, though not, it seems, nationally recognised names. Polly Toynbee is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The AfD’s win in Germany is a dark day for Europe. Time is running out to stop the far right | Cas Mudde
data.description: This party is among the most extreme in Europe. To protect our democracies, liberal parties must urgently change their tactics The far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) narrowly failed to secure an outright majority in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt. But nobody should take comfort from that. The party still won by a landslide. Decades of far-right election gains have made them seem normal to the point where only the biggest victories are deemed newsworthy. But 44% of the vote for a party that is officially classified as “extreme right” is not normal. It is a black day for European democracy, even if it occurs in a small east German state. While Saxony-Anhalt (and Germany itself) may have dodged the worst outcome because the AfD won’t automatically fulfil its ambition of forming the first far-right state government in Germany since the Nazi era, there is no reason to assume it will be so lucky at the next election. Neither will other German states, such as Mecklenburg-Vorpommern in two weeks’ time, or other countries, such as France next year. No country is immune from the far right and, perhaps even more worryingly, no far-right party or politician is too extreme for political success (as the US has shown). We must therefore update our analyses and strategies. Cas Mudde is the author of The Far Right Today, and is the Stanley Wade Shelton UGAF professor of international affairs at the University of Georgia Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on the far right’s real weapon: it is the politics of powerlessness | Editorial
data.description: From Dover to Saxony-Anhalt, extremists thrive when voters believe established parties can no longer deliver security, prosperity or meaningful change What links the thuggish masked agitation in southern England this weekend and the far-right Alternative für Deutschland’s (AfD) best-ever result in a German state – where it more than doubled the 21% vote it received five years ago? Several hundred men in balaclavas blocking an A road are not the same as a party winning a landslide election. But both events draw on the idea that the political system has lost control. The extremists in Dover and Portsmouth dramatise this claim; the electoral result in Germany threatens to institutionalise it. The prospect of Germany’s first far-right-led state government since the second world war carries real consequences. In Saxony-Anhalt it could see power handed to a party hostile to migrants, Islam, LGBTQ+ rights and climate policy. Alarmingly, it has senior figures linked to former neo-Nazi groups. About 170,000 foreign nationals live among 2 million people in Saxony-Anhalt – and roughly a fifth of the state’s doctors were born abroad. The grim paradox is that an AfD government could oversee the very state intelligence service that has classified the party as “ rightwing extremist ”. data.title: The Guardian view on skin cancer: fear the heat of the sun | Editorial
data.description: With melanoma cases rising, the UK must learn from public health campaigns elsewhere New climate risks bring with them new health risks. An exceptionally warm and dry summer in Europe meant that outdoor workers, and those who choose to spend leisure time in the sun, were confronted more directly than usual by the need to protect their skin from ultraviolet (UV) radiation, as well as avoid dehydration and overheating. In the UK, the annual total of new melanoma cases was reported to have risen above 20,000 for the first time earlier this year (the two most common forms of skin cancer, basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma, are less dangerous). As with other cancers, the increase in cases reflects an ageing and a growing population. A third of those diagnosed with cancer in the UK are over 75 . But with the NHS struggling to cope with the number of those seeking treatment, and melanoma the fifth most common cancer – after prostate, breast, lung and bowel (and excluding other skin cancers) – there are growing calls for behaviour change aligned to stronger public health measures. In May, a group of MPs proposed a ban on advertising sunbeds, which – along with sunburn and tanning – are linked with a raised risk of skin cancer. Last year, a group of experts advocated banning their commercial use altogether, as in Australia and Brazil. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? In the UK, the annual total of new melanoma cases was reported to have risen above 20,000 for the first time earlier this year (the two most common forms of skin cancer, basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma, are less dangerous). As with other cancers, the increase in cases reflects an ageing and a growing population. A third of those diagnosed with cancer in the UK are over 75 . But with the NHS struggling to cope with the number of those seeking treatment, and melanoma the fifth most common cancer – after prostate, breast, lung and bowel (and excluding other skin cancers) – there are growing calls for behaviour change aligned to stronger public health measures. In May, a group of MPs proposed a ban on advertising sunbeds, which – along with sunburn and tanning – are linked with a raised risk of skin cancer. Last year, a group of experts advocated banning their commercial use altogether, as in Australia and Brazil. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here . Continue reading...

data.title: Champions League is fertile ground for new managers – but knowhow could be key later on
data.description: Luis Enrique, Vincent Kompany and Mikel Arteta are among the favourites to lead their sides to victory, but more recent appointments should not be counted out A delve into the history of the Champions League shows that managers can and do win in their first season at a club, but also that experience matters. Which makes it interesting, given that tenures for the 2026‑27 crop range from newly appointed coaches to one with almost 15 years in charge. Some have managed more than 100 matches in the competition, others none. It gets under way on Tuesday with 14 of the 36 clubs led by managers who have been in the role for less than a year. It cannot match the turnover of the Premier League, in which 11 of 20 managers were appointed in 2026, but the tenures of the head coaches involved this season break down neatly. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It was very hurtful’: darts cult hero Stephen Bunting on death threats, social media – and the new Luke Littlers
data.description: The world No 10 on getting recognised in New York, coping with hostility and why he’s never changing his walk-on song “Definitely,” Stephen Bunting says as he considers whether working so hard as a darts player on social media is like making a deal with the devil. After Luke Littler, the prodigiously gifted teenage world champion , Bunting is the most heavily marketed player in darts. But, over the past year, some of his success on and off the oche has been accompanied by vicious abuse. Bunting has had death threats and he recently moved his eldest son to a private school to end the bullying which had hounded 14‑year‑old Toby, who often shares his social media space. But Bunting remains amiable and happy to reflect on his Faustian pact during a lucrative rollercoaster ride through darts. Continue reading...

data.title: Coco Gauff dismantles Iva Jovic to reach quarter-finals in confident US Open run
data.description: Gauff defeats Jovic 6-1, 6-4 in 80 minutes American has yet to drop a set in New York Andreeva awaits in anticipated quarter-final Coco Gauff continued her serene march through the US Open women’s draw with her most complete performance yet on Monday night, seeing off fellow American Iva Jovic 6-1, 6-4 to reach the last eight in New York for the first time since winning it all in her grand slam breakthrough three years ago. The fourth-seeded Gauff overwhelmed Jovic with the depth of her returns and an assured blend of aggression and defense, finishing with twice as many winners (18 to nine) and half as many unforced errors (15 to 30). The 1hr 20min clinic was the latest statement in a late-summer win streak that has transformed her from a player searching for answers this time last year into perhaps the most dangerous woman in the field right now. Continue reading...

data.title: Fake wide receivers to undercover stings: did the 49ers have the wildest NFL preseason of all time?
data.description: A large part of San Francisco’s summer was a literal car crash. On the positive side, they have so far avoided their usual list of crushing injuries The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers have trekked to Australia for this week’s NFL season opener in Melbourne. The flight time from California to Victoria is nearly the same for both teams – roughly 16 hours – but their journeys to the start of the season couldn’t be more different. It’s been smooth sailing for the Rams, with their collection of playmakers growing by the day . It’s a very different story for the 49ers: facing Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, not to mention the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks, at least twice this season is the least of their problems. Their offseason has been more than lightly turbulent: it’s been batshit crazy. Continue reading...

data.title: Bernie Ecclestone questioned after shotgun found on his private jet in Portugal
data.description: Former F1 chief says firearm was for clay-pigeon shooting Police quiz 95-year-old over lack of documents for gun Bernie Ecclestone was detained in Portugal on Monday after customs authorities found him in possession of an undocumented shotgun. The Guardian has independently confirmed the incident with multiple authorities involved in the matter. The detention of the 95‑year‑old took place at Tires Aerodrome in Cascais, shortly after the former Formula One chief’s private jet landed. After a routine inspection of the aircraft and its passengers, authorities reportedly discovered a shotgun in Ecclestone’s possession. He was stopped for questioning by Portuguese officials and said the gun was for use in clay pigeon shooting. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Safety, security and service’: behind the scenes with police at Arsenal v Chelsea
data.description: Facial recognition and spotters part of operation at Emirates that involved a dozen incidents and two arrests The concourses are silent when, deep in the Emirates Stadium’s bowels, Chief Inspector Pete Dearden’s briefing begins. Arsenal’s 4.30pm kick-off against Chelsea is still hours away but the fixture carries significance as a London derby and because the Premier League champions are hosting a realistic challenger. Dearden is a senior officer in the Metropolitan police’s public order command and Sunday’s matchday commander. He is, to borrow football jargon, giving the pre-match team talk, running through intelligence and in-game tactics. “Set the right style and tone,” he says. After Dearden has finished, the police room becomes a pseudo-station for the afternoon, with all incidents triaged by the same crime officer. Football offences can be found in niche legislation, and the Met wants London’s matchdays to be, so far as possible, policed uniformly. Continue reading...

data.title: Monaco kept their best players and are top of Ligue 1 – but at what cost?
data.description: You might think Monaco have plenty to cheer about, especially after their 2-1 win at PSG, but it’s complicated By Get French Football News When a manager says that “no player is more important than the club”, it is usually because said player is agitating for a move. Filipe Luís was referring to Folarin Balogun, who did quite the opposite on transfer deadline day, opting to stay at Monaco rather than joining Everton, despite an agreement between the clubs. You’d think that retaining your top scorer from last season would be reason for celebration, but the fact it is not once again exposes the French football paradox. Like plenty of other clubs in Ligue 1, Monaco are torn between sporting and financial prerogatives. They ended up prioritising the former on transfer deadline day, albeit unwillingly, and even in a week when they beat PSG at the Parc des Princes to retain their 100% record, it is bittersweet. Continue reading...

data.title: Karius keeps Kane at bay as Schalke nullify Bayern on Neuer’s return | Andy Brassell
data.description: The often-derided Loris Karius upstaged Manuel Neuer as Schalke held Bayern to a rare goalless draw in a tale of two goalkeepers in Gelsenkirchen If one goalkeeper was going to dominate the discussion in this game, it actually felt as if it would be the less busy one. Schalke fans do not take kindly to being dumped and even if Manuel Neuer left the club behind 15 years ago – and even if most of the world associates him with Bayern Munich rather than his home town club – he is still given a rough ride when he returns. Opposing sporting directors Max Eberl and Frank Baumann had words to say about that after Saturday evening’s latest visit, but it wasn’t Germany’s legendary goalkeeper who took the headlines – or not he alone, at least. It was always going to be a landmark afternoon with Schalke playing a first home game in the top flight since May 2023, but this was way beyond what anyone could have expected. The numbers said it all – with Bayern failing to score for the first time domestically since a goalless draw at Leverkusen more than 18 months ago, meaning they finished the weekend not on top of the table for the first time in almost two years – but told nothing of the story. Continue reading...

data.title: England’s teenagers outperform peers in most countries in maths, reading and science
data.description: OECD test sees results dip in almost all member nations and warns of ‘digital distractions’ eroding academic skills England’s teenagers are outperforming their peers in most countries in maths, reading and science, according to an international survey that warns of “digital distractions” eroding academic skills around the world. The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) programme for international student assessment (Pisa), which last year tested 760,000 15-year-olds in 91 countries and regions, found that results dipped in almost all of its members compared with previous years, with the exception of England and a handful of others. Continue reading...

data.description: Minister condemns groups behind Hampshire disorder and says officers were injured as they repelled ‘aggression’ Batons and synthetic pepper spray were used to repel hundreds of masked, black-clad vigilantes in Portsmouth on Sunday, it has emerged, as the policing minister said officers had been injured as they repelled organised “aggression”. After police contained the weekend’s second disruptive demonstration against asylum seekers travelling to the UK in small boats, it was claimed that officers in Hampshire were pushed off their motorbikes and pelted with bricks. Sarah Jones, the Home Office minister, condemned groups behind the disorder for promoting “racism and thuggery”. Continue reading...

In the latest sign that Japan’s patience with mass tourism is wearing thin, Shinjuku ward – home to the notorious Kabukicho nightlife district and the world’s busiest railway station – will prevent visitors from using private lodgings in residential areas and near schools and important cultural sites, Japanese media reported this week. data.title: Canada’s retaliatory US tariffs take effect as trade dispute grows
data.description: Counter-measures covering several sectors come after Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian goods Canada’s retaliatory tariffs on billions of dollars’ worth of American imports have come into effect, escalating a trade fight that has been marked by intensifying tensions between US president Donald Trump and Canadian prime minister Mark Carney. The tariffs took effect at 12.01am on Tuesday, and range from 15% to 50% and apply to products covering $20bn in imports from the US. The measures target sectors including steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics – industries that have been most affected by US tariffs. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘We have really cool sharks’: three-year project to lift lid on Britain’s little-understood species
data.description: Anglers will help scientists investigate the porbeagle, tope and blue shark to boost knowledge and conservation ‘We have really cool sharks,” says Dr Lucy Hawkes. She is not referring to animals in the rich coastal waters of South Africa or Mexico, but instead talking about the species that live around Britain. Hawkes, an associate professor at the University of Exeter, is co-leading a new three-year project to investigate the lives of three of England’s most vulnerable shark species. “I like the porbeagle, which looks like a baby great white shark,” she says. “Surfers could see one and absolutely poop their pants, but they’re not dangerous. It’s amazing that we share the water with some pretty exciting animals.” Continue reading...

data.title: Cities in Great Britain most vulnerable to extreme heat revealed
data.description: OS index examines which ‘urban heat islands’ suffer the most – and which cope the best with rising temperatures Portsmouth, Leicester, Exeter, Bristol and Nottingham will be among the cities that warm the most by the end of this century as global heating turns British cities into urban heat islands, according to research. Analysis from Ordnance Survey (OS) has created a heat vulnerability index for all cities in Great Britain. Portsmouth, which sits on the south coast of England and is home to 208,000 people, is the most vulnerable to extreme heat today and into the future, according to the research from the OS, the Met Office and the data analysis company 4 Earth Intelligence. Continue reading...

data.description: James Frith says patients may be less willing to share data as new figures show a rise in opt-outs Concern is being raised about Palantir’s work with the NHS as new figures showed tens of thousands of patients have withdrawn their data from use in research projects. data.title: US woman charged with killing son ‘very invested’ in Lindsay Clancy trial, prosecutors say
data.description: Corie Walsh charged with murder after two-year-old Barrett found dead in basement of Illinois family home last week An Illinois woman charged with killing her two-year-old son had been closely following the murder trial of Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy and was texting friends about the case just hours before her son was found dead, prosecutors said. data.title: ‘Trust deficit’: Why India’s economic data has sparked a furore
data.description: India’s statistical system once commanded respect, and its data on economic and social indicators was considered rigorous – that appears to have eroded • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here There isn’t much that we Indians agree on these days. GDP numbers are no exception. Last week, India released glowing GDP numbers for the latest quarter – 7.8% growth – higher than the forecast 7% . It sparked a furore. Subhash Garg, a former finance secretary under Narendra Modi’s government and now a critic, reframed what Modi called a “herculean feat” as mere smoke and mirrors. According to Garg , the government revised last year’s current-price GDP downwards to inflate this year’s number – he believes the real growth is only 2.6%. Continue reading...

data.title: The Newer World by Sebastian Barry review – a near-miracle of storytelling
data.description: The third in a loose American trilogy follows the epic journey of a formerly enslaved man in the aftermath of the civil war But is not the story as good as the truth?” asks Tennyson Bouguereau, the narrator of Sebastian Barry’s The Newer World. Tennyson, a formerly enslaved man in post-civil war America, recounts his life story in ways that call to mind the age-old debate about whether it’s better to get our history from novelists or historians. While historians might argue that there is no contest, the question hints knowingly at the novelist’s counter-argument. It sent me searching for a line from Barry’s 2008 Costa-award winning novel, The Secret Scripture , in which the narrator describes history as “a fabulous arrangement of surmises and guesses held up as a banner against the assault of withering truth”. In her Reith Lectures, Hilary Mantel suggested that history is “what’s left in the sieve when the centuries have run through it”, but I tend to think of it as more of a butterfly net. Historians chase after and capture the things they deem significant. They leave things out, often deliberately. Barry’s entire body of work is a prime example of fiction’s ability to fill history’s gaps, merging personal tragedies with national ones in ways that (dare I say) demonstrate the supremacy of the form – especially for those of us descended from people for whom history never cared one whit. I was therefore intrigued to learn that he had set out to write the story of a man like Tennyson. Barry’s earlier novels refracted Irish history through the lens of two fictional Irish families, the Dunnes and the McNultys. His first foray into this period of American history in Days Without End , for which he won his second Costa award, also followed one of the McNultys – Thomas McNulty flees the Irish famine for America, where he finds himself drawn into the genocidal work of clearing Native Americans off their land, and then, together with his lover and fellow soldier, John Cole, adopts a Lakota girl, Winona, whose family they have helped slaughter. Barry picked up Winona’s story in A Thousand Moons , published in 2020, which follows her fortunes as she, Thomas and John settle on the same farm outside Paris, Tennessee that is occupied by Tennyson and his twin sister Rosalee among others. Continue reading...

data.title: Can breath be art? Liz Larner on sculpting with hair, lashes, leather – and international group exhalation
data.description: The Californian once cultivated petri dishes breathed on by artists that turned ‘murky and scary’. But now, in our dystopian age of space technocrats, she’s taking inspiration from Nasa shots of asteroids ‘I had artists from all over the world breathe over petri dishes,” says Liz Larner. “It was a piece of international art made from breath bacteria.” The American sculptor is reminiscing about her 1988 work Every Artist Gave a Breath, a fragile and strangely evolving work of art grown on agar. Exhibited in a 2022 show, it has since transformed in various ways: some bacteria has morphed into “beautiful, dried wafers in colour”, while other dishes “turned into a really weird blackish-green, really murky and a little scary”. Larner is no stranger to making alluring work out of strange materials, from human hair and false eyelashes to leather and surgical gauze. For her first major exhibition in the UK – A Hard Line to Bend at Camden Arts Centre in London – the sculptor has been transforming single-use plastic into pieces that bristle with seductiveness and menace. “I was living in LA at the time when China stopped accepting American plastic, which was where we were sending it all to be recycled,” she says. “I started taking it to my studio – it got so huge, I had to hang it from my ceiling.” Continue reading...

data.title: TV has never been so nerve-jangling: 10 years of the agonising Motherland
data.description: The rage, the wine, the power mums, the PTA horror – the BBC sitcom was a spot on send-up of life at the school gates. A decade on, we remember its most awkward bits If Uncut Gems was about the school run instead of gambling debts, it would look like Motherland. It is now 10 years since the BBC sitcom jangled the already frayed nerves of all parents watching and turned Anna Maxwell Martin into the most frazzled woman on television in the name of skewering middle-class motherhood. Whether she was marching her children to buy school shoes the night before term started (“Don’t be closed. Pleeeeeaaaaase don’t be closed”) or having a meltdown at temporary traffic lights en route to a school drop-off that proved redundant because she’d forgotten it was half-term, Maxwell Martin’s Julia would undoubtedly have a more chilled-out time in the kitchen of The Bear than raising her kids. Continue reading...

data.title: Better Go Mad in the Wild review – boozing, bantering hermits impart their spiritual wisdom
data.description: Director Miro Remo journeys deep into the Czech countryside to find two brothers living an isolated life filled with quixotic wisdom in this surreal documentary Narrated by a slaughtered bull, this extraordinary film takes the less-travelled path in charting the daily life of a pair of Czech twins a long way off conventional routes themselves. František and Ondřej Klišík are slowly going mad – or maybe closing in on enlightenment – in a cabin in the Šumava mountains and, extrapolating a short story about the brothers by Aleš Palán, director Miro Remo succumbs productively to the prevailing cabin fever – not only egging these longbeards on in their squabbling and loopy philosophising, but pitching in with his own fabulism and surrealism. Closing on 60, “Franta” and “Ondra” still farm their smallholding with the help of Nandy, a mutinous bull ill-chosen as a draught animal. In their downtime, they booze, banter and bicker, lament their lack of prospects with the fairer sex, and blow off steam in epic arm-wrestling bouts. Despite an arm lost to a sawmill accident, it’s Franta who’s usually the victor; he is also possessed by a quixotic streak absent in his bluff sibling. Letting loose streams of poetry into the air like bunting, wishing “joy to all conscious beings”, he is also constructing his own Da Vinci-style perpetual flying machine. “Your aversion to my perpetuum is a little annoying,” he informs the exasperated Ondra. Continue reading...

data.title: End of the Road festival review – Pulp and CMAT lead indie landmark’s joyous birthday party
data.description: Larmer Tree Gardens, Wiltshire Hitting 20, this festival has grown into a warm, genre-hopping powerhouse where fringe experimental acts are greeted as warmly as the star headliners There is a celebratory feeling in the air at End of the Road festival this year as it turns 20. The piano stage has been turned into a giant birthday cake with candles on top, one man is dressed as a toilet to commemorate the porcelain anniversary, and Jarvis Cocker leads a spirited singalong of Happy Birthday while wishing for 20 more years. Retaining a core identity while also expanding and evolving has been key to that longevity. While early days were centred more on alt-folk and Americana, EOTR is now a genre-hopping powerhouse, blending everything from pop fun to noisy experimentation via global grooves, and with an equal focus on the familiar and the unknown. Continue reading...

data.title: Gloria Steinem’s revolutionary life – podcast
data.description: From going undercover as a Playboy bunny to founding Ms Magazine, Steinem brought feminism into the US mainstream. Carter Sherman explains her legacy By the time she died last week at the age of 92, Gloria Steinem had become almost synonymous with the modern feminist movement in the US. The arc of Steinem’s life – and activism – was a long one. From going undercover as a Playboy bunny to becoming a radical publisher bringing feminism into the mainstream. She was a fearless reproductive rights campaigner. In Ms Magazine she wrote about having an abortion – and encouraged other famous women, and readers, to do the same to break the stigma around it. Continue reading...

data.title: Oasis recordings up for auction despite band’s objections
data.description: Guide price of archive documenting concerts, rehearsals, soundchecks and conversations between £1.2m and £1.6m An archive of more than 100 hours of Oasis recordings, including concerts, rehearsals and candid conversations between Noel and Liam Gallagher, is to be auctioned for up to £1.6m despite objections from the band. The collection was amassed by the band’s sound engineer Huw Richards, who worked with Oasis from the release of their 1994 debut album, Definitely Maybe, until 2001. It comprises 209 DAT tapes, 73 analogue cassettes and three MiniDiscs, and is being sold by Richards’s son, Owain. Continue reading...

data.description: Who’s more likely to steal sweets from a child? According to science, it’s the rich. data.title: José Pizarro’s recipe for grilled sardines with blackberry escabeche
data.description: A winning combination of oily fish, sweet berries and a sharp dressing One of my favourite summer memories is making collares de moras as a child in Extremadura, which involved threading wild blackberries on to a piece of straw to make little necklaces. We’d always eat some too, of course, as well as wearing them, and we’d always come home with stained hands and big smiles. At the time, I never imagined that one day I’d be cooking sardines and pairing them with those same wild berries, but that’s the magic of food. The ingredients that filled my childhood with such simple joy have become part of the dishes I love creating today. Every time I make this recipe, it takes me straight back to those carefree summer days. Continue reading...

data.title: Cravings ‘like heroin withdrawal’: what happens when weight-loss drugs don’t work?
data.description: GLP-1 medications have been a gamechanger in the fight against obesity. But for a minority of patients, their impact is negligible. Why? When Mercedes was told by her doctor that she could be prescribed GLP-1 weight loss jabs in 2024, she broke down. “[When] she said yes, I cried in her office. And I didn’t really stop crying for a week,” she said. “Finally, after being overweight my entire life, this was going to save me. My struggle, my burden, my shame was finally going to come to an end.” Continue reading...

data.title: A job that changed me: I went off the rails in school and worked nights at a blast furnace. It was like gazing into the fiery pit of hell
data.description: It finally dawned on me that perhaps the teachers were not just getting in the way of my good times, they were actually on my side I arrived in Australia from the UK in 1983, at the sprightly age of 14. Unbeknown to me I was a historical figure, the very last of the £10 poms. My parents and I were a family full of beans about a new life but just over a year later tragedy struck when my mother was killed in a car crash. My father and I were left to carry each other in grief. We were wildly unprepared. At only 35, my dad did his best to solo-parent while at school I went off the rails – all booze, sex and drugs. I couldn’t care less about education, had no interest in what lay beyond schooling and crashed out of year 12 with no grades. Continue reading...

data.title: 25 years ago, two strangers met in the twin towers and escaped on 9/11. What happened next?
data.description: Stanley Praimnath and Brian Clark were two of only four individuals known to have survived above the impact zone in the south tower He has told the story hundreds of times, but it never seems to fade. If anything, it only becomes more vivid. “Oh, gosh,” exclaims Stanley Praimnath, his voice cracking with an “ooooooh!” as if bearing a weight. “It’s like reliving that day.” Nearly 3,000 people died in the terrorist attacks on New York City and Washington DC on September 11 2001. But Praimnath and another office worker, Brian Clark, were two of only four individuals known to have survived from above the impact zone in either tower of the World Trade Center. The two strangers met in the smoke and fire of the 81st floor of the south tower, and walked down 1,620 steps into the rest of their lives. Continue reading...

data.title: Europe’s centre fears nationalist wave after AfD victory but only has itself to blame
data.description: Saxony-Anhalt win part of wider trend driven by mainstream policy failures and gradual normalisation of far right ideas The numbers speak for themselves: Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), a party that dabbles in Nazi imagery, distinguishes between “biological” and “passport” Germans, and is too extreme even for France’s far-right leader Marine Le Pen, nearly doubled its score in Sunday’s state election in Saxony-Anhalt to 43.8% of the vote. Meanwhile, the centre-right CDU of the chancellor, Friedrich Merz, collapsed to 17.2%, less than half its total in the same race five years ago, and the centre-left SPD – Germany’s other main party of government for the past 60-odd years – scraped 9.3%. The least that can be said is that the centre did not hold. Continue reading...

data.title: Mozart's melodies were less predictable, teen finds
data.description: Eighteen-year-old Linus Chen-Plotkin from Philadelphia has created a groundbreaking study on the genius of Mozart. This unique characteristic allowed him to both adhere to classical standards and surprise his audience, offering fresh insights into the nature of musical innovation and the essence of artistic excellence.

data.title: In 1895, lightning ignited a West Virginia gas well; flames soared 200 feet as crowds watched
data.description: In a remarkable display, a West Virginia gas well suffered a fiery explosion triggered by a lightning strike. Discovered in 1895, this vast gas reservoir was tough to control with the limited technology of the era. For two hours, flames leaped 150 to 200 feet into the sky until the force of the escaping gas extinguished itself.

data.title: Whistleblower Part 2: The redemption of Floyd Landis
data.description: The fall of Lance Armstrong was intertwined with the similarly disgraced descent of his one-time American Postal teammate Floyd Landis. Landis, having come from a unique rural and religious background, rose through the ranks to take the coveted Tour de France title for himself just one year after Armstrong stood adorned in the famous yellow jersey as a record-breaker en route to retirement and the continued adulation of millions who bought into his story of triumph over tragedy.In time, both men would be exposed as doping cheats after Landis confessed to what many had suspected, and indeed accused of, for years – creating the domino effect that would ultimately bring Armstrong down. Twenty years on from his tainted victory in 2006, Landis still has a lot to say, and the Sunday Independent’s Paul Kimmage was on hand to hear it. On the conclusion of a two-part Indo Daily special, we outline why Landis denied the truth for years, the fallout from his eventual admission, and how his story had to come all the way back to the start in order to find a new way forward. Host: Fionnán Sheahan Guest: Paul Kimmage The Indo Daily is part of the Trust Project. See our ethics policies at independent.ie/ourjournalism Paul Kimmage’s three-part ‘Cheat or Be Cheated’ documentary can be watched on the Irish Independent YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D54sDw_M1nw And you can read the full 35,000-word transcript of his original 2010 interview with Floyd Landis here: https://nyvelocity.com/articles/interviews/landiskimmage/

De son côté, l’Alternative pour l’Allemagne affirme vouloir atteindre 40 % des suffrages au niveau fédéral en 2029.

data.title: La tour Eiffel a rouvert après une grève contre l’éviction du personnel féminin lors de la visite d’une délégation hindoue
data.description: La société d’exploitation du site a reconnu que la délégation hindoue avait demandé une visite qui limite les « interactions avec les femmes ». Le maire de Paris a promis une enquête « dans les plus brefs délais ».

data.title: New York Times: inwoners stad voorgelogen over luchtkwaliteit na 9/11

data.title: Na maanden weerstand gaat Volkswagen-fabriek in het Duitse Osnabrück nu toch Israëlische wapens produceren
data.description: Een Israëlisch investeringsfonds en de Duitse deelstaat Nedersaksen kopen een fabriek van Volkswagen op. data.title: Zwrot kaucji nie tylko pod marketem. Specjalne butelkomaty staną na osiedlach
data.description: Na osiedlach, terenach spółdzielni i wspólnot mieszkaniowych w ciągu najbliższych kilku lat pojawią się tysiące butelkomatów. Urządzenia będą zwracać kaucję bezpośrednio na kartę płatniczą. Operatorzy chcą w ten sposób uprościć proces oddawania opakowań i uniezależnić go od wizyty w konkretnym sklepie.

data.title: Tragiczny finał poszukiwań Polaka na Słowacji. 27-latek nie żyje
data.description: Nie żyje 27-letni Polak, który zaginął podczas wycieczki w słowackich Tatrach Wysokich. Jego ciało odnaleziono na północnej ścianie Szerokiej Wieży. Jak informuje Polsat News, w akcji poszukiwawczej uczestniczyli ratownicy górscy, operatorzy dronów, przewodnicy z psami tropiącymi oraz załoga śmigłowca.

data.title: Červený promluví k úniku toxických látek na Šumavě
data.description: Na území národního parku Šumava podle ministra životního prostřední za Motoristy Igora Červeného unikají do půdy toxické látky po působení armády. Podrobnosti mají zaznít v úterý na tiskové konferenci na resortu obrany, kde ministr zároveň představí časový plán řešení situace. Červený v pondělí uvedl, že škodlivé látky pocházejí z někdejšího působení armády a kontaminují půdu i okolí. Tiskovou konferenci nabídne iDNES.cz živě.

data.title: Vlak u Hostivaře srazil člověka, na místě zemřel. Provoz na koridoru je omezený
data.description: Na železničním koridoru mezi Prahou a Benešovem v úseku mezi pražskou Hostivaří a Uhříněvsí srazil vlak člověka, střet nepřežil. data.title: Poslance čeká opět boj o zákon o státních zaměstnancích, návrh vrátil Senát
data.description: Poslanci budou znovu schvalovat změny v podmínkách zaměstnávání státních úředníků. Zákon o státních zaměstnancích odmítli senátoři kvůli obavám z politizace státní správy. Vetovali i doprovodnou novelu, kterou chtějí ANO, SPD a Motoristé sobě omezit pravomoci prezidenta při pověřování a odvolávání vedoucích stálých misí u mezinárodních organizací. Pravomoc má získat ministr zahraničí.

data.title: Slapy denně klesají o 20 centimetrů. Brzy mohou být pod úrovní běžnou pro zimu
data.description: Pokles hladiny Slapské přehrady bude podle aktuálních předpovědí minimálně v nejbližších dnech pokračovat, a to přibližně o 20 centimetrů denně. Zásobní prostor je naplněný z 89 procent. Pokud bude přetrvávat nynější hydrologický vývoj, zhruba za týden by mohla hladina přehrady klesnout pod úroveň pro zimní období, řekla dnes Jaroslava Vedlová ze sekretariátu generálního ředitele Povodí Vltavy.

data.title: Lidojed v nové Kriminálce Anděl měl svůj předobraz. Byl mnohem děsivější
data.description: Krimiseriály bývají inspirované skutečnými případy, většinou je ale vyhrocují, aby byly působivější, temnější a senzačnější. U nejnovějšího dílu Kriminálky Anděl s názvem Lidojed je to ale naopak. S případem slovenského vraha a patrně i kanibala Matěje Čurka má společné jen některé motivy. Skutečnost byla mnohem, mnohem děsivější.

data.title: Jelena střelil cizinec z auta a bez povolení. Soud mu vzal pušku a vyměřil pokutu
data.description: Na loveckou vášeň doplatil osmačtyřicetiletý cizinec. Při návratu z legálního lovu na Chebsku střelil u Křepkovic jelena siku, který stál u silnice. Ani se při tom neobtěžoval vystoupit z auta. Policie ho obvinila z pytláctví a pokusu o krádež. Soud mu zabavil zbraň a vyměřil pokutu.

data.title: KOMENTÁŘ: Filmové Benátky konečně objevují, že existují dvě Ruska. Možná tři
data.description: Hvězdný herec George Clooney tu převzal čestnou cenu, ale do popředí 83. festivalu v Benátkách se dostal jiný, méně známý muž. Jmenuje se Ilja Chržanovskij, jeho film Dau přijali do hlavní soutěže, Ukrajina proti tomu protestovala a celý filmový svět teď řeší, jestli je režisér Rus, respektive Dau film ruský, potažmo proruský, zkrátka putinovský.

data.title: Na jižní Moravě bude step a v Praze čekejte až 47 stupňů Celsia, varuje Cílek
data.description: Podle geologa a spisovatele Václava Cílka čeká Prahu teplota až 47 stupňů Celsia kvůli kumulaci tepla, zatímco jižní Moravě hrozí kvůli erozi černozemě přeměna na step. V pořadu Rozstřel na iDNES.cz mluvil i o tom, kolik vody z krajiny mizí, proč přijdou povodně a jak se má Česko připravit na klimatickou změnu.

data.title: Po výhrůžce v Kadani evakuovali i ležící pacienty. Čin ubožáka, píše starosta
data.description: Policisté kvůli anonymní výhrůžce bombou evakuovali nemocnici v Kadani na Chomutovsku, museli ji opustit i pacienti, kteří jsou na lůžku. Na místo dorazil pyrotechnik a kynolog se psem specializovaným na vyhledávání výbušnin. Kolem 9:15 policie oznámila, že žádnou bombu nenašla.

data.title: Lídry EU šokoval pohřeb Mladiče. Zpochybnili cestu Srbska do Unie
data.description: Záběry z pondělního pohřbu odsouzeného válečného zločince Ratka Mladiče byly podle šéfky Evropské komise i předsedy Evropské rady šokující. Přítomnost některých vysokých srbských představitelů na pohřbu označili za politováníhodnou a v rozporu s hodnotami, které jsou důležité na cestě Srbska do Evropské unie. Ursula von der Leyenová a António Costa to uvedli ve společném prohlášení.

data.title: Ve Francii ukradli Renoirovy obrazy, kamery zachytily dva zloděje
data.description: Z muzea Pierra-Augusta Renoira v Cagnes-sur-Mer na jihovýchodě Francie byla ukradena nejméně čtyři díla. Bezpečnostní kamery v noci na úterý zachytily dva lupiče, jak obrazy odřezávají. Jedno z ukradených děl na útěku upustili. Starosta města Bryan Masson odhadl hodnotu lupu na devět milionů eur (asi 218 milionů korun).

data.title: Po 11. září ovládla New York islamofobie, teď si muslimové berou město zpět
data.description: Asadu Dandiovi bylo osm let, když útoky 11. září 2001 sledoval v televizi doma u rodičů, pákistánských imigrantů v New Yorku. Poté následovala vlna nevraživosti – roky islamofobie, jak se Američané vyrovnávali s útoky, při nichž přišlo o život téměř 3000 lidí, a projevoval se vztek, podezíravost a horší věci. Nyní muslimové ve městě opět posilují svou pozici.

data.title: Mohutný požár pohltil obchodní dům Lidl v Kladně
data.description: Hasiči v noci likvidovali mohutný požár obchodního domu Lidl v Kladně. Vyhlásili druhý a později i třetí stupeň poplachu, na místě zasahovalo na 18 jednotek. Z přilehlé ubytovny evakuovali 53 lidí. Požár se jim podařilo dostat pod kontrolu po 2. hodině ranní.

data.title: Jakub Štáfek s dlouhými dredy? V černé komedii se představí jako šipkař Milánek
data.description: Pepé má pouhých 48 hodin na to, aby si zachránil život. Jediným člověkem, který mu může pomoci, je Milánek – šílený šipkařský génius, jenž však před lidmi netrefí ani terč. Nová komedie Šipkaři kombinuje černý humor, akci a kriminální zápletku s pořádnou dávkou absurdity. Ve filmu z prostředí šipkařských turnajů a zapadlých hospod dostali hlavní role Tomáš Maštalír a Jakub Štáfek. Premiéru plánují na 8. října.

data.title: Manželé v Polsku vyhodili s komodou i životní úspory. Nálezci teď hrozí vězení
data.description: Ztrátou životních úspor mohli za chvilku nepozornosti zaplatit obyvatelé polské vsi Warzymice u Štětína, kteří spolu se starou komodou vyhodili i několik desítek tisíc eur v hodnotě přesahující milion korun. data.title: Šumavu otravují toxické látky po armádě. Turek mluvil o yperitu, pak o fosgenu
data.description: Na území národního parku Šumava podle ministra životního prostředí za Motoristy sobě Igora Červeného unikají do půdy toxické látky po působení armády, které kontaminují i okolí. Oznámil to na tiskové konferenci po pondělním jednání vlády. Poslanec za Motoristy Filip Turek mluvil nejprve o yperitu, následně se opravil, že jde o fosgen. Pak své vyjádření korigoval znovu.

data.title: Ukrajina chce převzít výrobce balené vody. Vadí jí podíl ruského oligarchy
data.description: Ukrajinské úřady vedou spor s britskou miliardářskou rodinou Patarkacišviliových o budoucnost významného výrobce balené vody IDS Ukraine. Společnost, pod kterou patří nejprodávanější ukrajinská značka balené vody Moršinska, částečně vlastní ruští investoři včetně oligarchy Michaila Fridmana. Právě kvůli Rusům ukrajinské úřady v roce 2022 majetkové podíly ve společnosti zmrazily.

data.title: Pražská burza doufá v příval kapitálu. Startuje první české ETF
data.description: Desítka největších českých akcií je nově k dostání v jednom košíku. Pražská burza má za sebou historický zlom. Od včerejška si investoři mohou pořídit první tuzemský burzovně obchodovaný fond, který pasivně kopíruje hlavní index pražské burzy. Měl by usnadnit investice do českých firem veřejnosti i zahraničním investorům. Ti už nemusejí kupovat jednotlivé akcie zvlášť, ale mohou si pod zkratkou WOOD PX ETF zakoupit naráz celý koš největších firem.

data.title: Koalice směřuje k dohodě. Může se vrátit, že se v prvních dnech stoná zadarmo
data.description: Vládní koalice ANO, SPD a Motoristů sobě směřuje podle ministra pro sport, prevenci a zdraví za Motoristy sobě Borise Šťastného k dohodě, která by vedla k tomu, že by se v řádu miliard podařilo snížit schodek státního rozpočtu navržený na příští rok ve výši 389 miliard korun. „Směřujeme k tomu, aby skutečně ten schodek byl nižší, respektive závěrečný účet byl nižší,“ řekl Šťastný.

data.title: Los data centers, el nuevo punto de fricción en las elecciones de EE UU

La clave de la disputa no es frenar la infraestructura, sino definir si las tecnológicas pagarán su expansión o si los costos se trasladarán a los consumidores. data.title: MRC : la diaspora Europe réaffirme son soutien sans faille à Maurice Kamto
data.description: © DR Dans une déclaration datée du 6 septembre 2026, les secrétaires départementaux MRC de la Région Europe apportent un soutien "éclairé et lucide" à leur président national élu, Maurice Kamto, au directoire et aux résolutions du Conseil national du 6 septembre 2025. A un peu plus d'un an après l'exclusion de Maurice Kamto de la course à la présidentielle du 12 octobre 2025, la fédération Europe du Mouvement pour la Renaissance du Cameroun (MRC) sort du silence. Dans un texte de deux pages signé collectivement, les responsables départementaux dénoncent ce qu'ils qualifient d'acharnement politico-judiciaire contre leur leader et contre le parti. "Notre parti dont vous tenez courageusement et avec brio le flambeau depuis la création, fait l'objet depuis toujours d'actes de déstabilisation de la part du pouvoir en place et de ses proxys", écrivent-ils à l'adresse de Maurice Kamto. L'exclusion de 2025 au cœur de la déclaration Le communiqué revient longuement sur l'invalidation de la candidature de Maurice Kamto à la présidentielle de 2025, officialisée le 5 août 2025 par le Conseil constitutionnel après un rejet initial par ELECAM pour "pluralité d'investitures" au sein du MANIDEM. Pour les signataires, cette décision est le fruit "d'un acte de cybercriminalité du MINAT" et d'un "complot d'Etat" contre le MRC. Ils citent notamment deux correspondances du ministère de l'Administration territoriale adressées à M. Thierry Okala Ebode, présenté comme un ancien militant exclu pour trahison, et au secrétaire général du parti. Une contre-attaque contre le RDPC Le texte opère un renversement d'accusation. Les secrétaires Europe rappellent que depuis juillet 2025, un militant du RDPC a officiellement saisi le MINAT, Paul Atanga Nji, de l'illégalité de toutes les instances dirigeantes de son propre parti, dont le dernier Congrès remonte à septembre 2011. Une saisine portée ensuite devant le Tribunal de grande instance du Mfoundi pour faire juger "nulles et de nul effet" les résolutions du Bureau politique du 3 novembre 2016. "Curieusement, ni le MINAT, militant du RDPC, ni le président du tribunal [...] n'a jugé utile de donner suite à sa saisine", souligne la déclaration. Et d'interroger : "Pourquoi donc tant d'agitation du RDPC et de ses prolongements étatiques contre le MRC et son Président National Elu, que vous êtes, alors que, sans avoir, enfin, organisé son Congrès [...] toutes les candidatures du RDPC vont logiquement être rejetées ?" Cap sur les législatives et municipales Au-delà de la dénonciation, le message est un appel à la mobilisation. Les responsables Europe disent faire "totalement confiance à l'intelligence des membres du directoire’’ et à leur président ‘’pour déjouer la nouvelle forfaiture du pouvoir en cours". Ils invitent Maurice Kamto et le directoire à "rester concentrés sur l'essentiel, la préparation victorieuse des élections législatives et municipales à venir" et appellent "tous les dynamiques et courageux militants à persister, avec vous et contre vents et marées". Une déclaration qui se conclut sur une profession de foi en "la vision humaniste, moderniste, développée, fondée sur le mérite, la solidarité, l'état de droit, la justice du MRC", portée selon eux par un leader "aimé par les Camerounais’’. Cet article MRC : la diaspora Europe réaffirme son soutien sans faille à Maurice Kamto est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Création du poste de vice-président au Cameroun : ‘’Toute controverse orchestrée par des acteurs politiques … est vaine’’, Paul Atanga Nji
data.description: © DR Dans une tribune publiée dans le quotidien The Guardian Post paru ce 07 septembre, le ministre de l’Administration territoriale, Paul Atanga Nji, veut faire taire les controverses autour de la restauration du poste de vice-président au Cameroun. Pour lui, ‘’il est temps de mettre fin à la chasse aux sorcières concernant le poste de Vice-Président’’. Lire un extrait de sa tribune… ‘’Lors de sa cérémonie de prestation de serment, le 6 novembre 2025, le chef de l’État, Son Excellence Paul Biya, le Grand Visionnaire, avait déclaré : « Nous devons également soumettre au Parlement certaines réformes qui permettront à l’État de fonctionner plus efficacement, en adaptant nos institutions aux exigences de notre environnement. » Comme toujours, le chef de l’État dit ce qu’il fait et fait ce qu’il dit. Ainsi, S.E. Paul Biya a présenté devant le Parlement, qui siégeait en mars 2026, un projet de loi visant à modifier la Constitution. Le principal changement était la création du poste de Vice-Président de la République. Au lieu de saluer cette innovation majeure dans le fonctionnement de nos institutions, certains dirigeants de l’opposition, soutenus par les médias et des ONG agissant sur ordre, alimentent d’étranges débats dans le but de la discréditer. Il se dit qu’un homme politique, victime de ses propres méfaits, aurait adressé une pétition à l’Union africaine (UA) pour s’opposer à la création du poste de Vice-Président. Certains parlent de l’introduction d’un ticket présidentiel dans l’élection présidentielle. Pourquoi le Cameroun devrait-il se préoccuper de ce qui se passe ailleurs ? Le président Paul Biya n’avait-il pas déjà averti que « le Cameroun est… » … « le Cameroun », un pays maître de son propre destin, qui ne suit pas aveuglément les autres sans tenir compte de ses propres réalités ? En ma qualité de ministre de l’Administration territoriale, j’ai eu le privilège de présenter au Sénat et à l’Assemblée nationale, réunis en session conjointe, les amendements au Code électoral relatifs à la création du poste de Vice-Président de la République. J’ai expliqué aux élus de la nation les mérites de l’initiative du chef de l’État. Les membres de l’Assemblée nationale et du Sénat ont adopté les projets de loi du gouvernement à une très large majorité. Conformément aux dispositions légales en vigueur, les textes ont été promulgués par le chef de l’État. Toute controverse orchestrée par des acteurs politiques — principalement ceux de l’opposition — est vaine. Je pense qu’il est temps de mettre fin à la chasse aux sorcières concernant le poste de Vice-Président. La politique de la nation est définie par le chef de l’État. En vertu de ses prérogatives et de son pouvoir discrétionnaire, le chef de l’État nomme des personnes à des fonctions civiles et militaires et peut relever de leurs fonctions les personnes nommées à tout moment. Ces dispositions sont inscrites dans la Constitution et doivent être prises en compte. De plus, Son Excellence Paul Biya connaît le Cameroun mieux que chacun d’entre nous. Je mets quiconque au défi de me prouver le contraire. Dans mon livre, publié avant l’élection présidentielle du 12 octobre 2025 et intitulé « 37 Years of Unwavering Loyalty to the Head of State. Understanding the Meaning of My Ongoing Struggle for Respect for Republican Legality », j’ai souligné que trop d’événements avaient démontré que le chef de l’État avait raison. Il est dans notre intérêt de suivre la voie tracée par Son Excellence Paul Biya, qui a plus de 30 ans d’avance sur nous tous — hauts responsables de la République, hommes politiques, dirigeants de la société civile et autres. Son Excellence Paul Biya possède cette capacité extraordinaire de voir aujourd’hui les obstacles que nous autres, et particulièrement ceux qui font du bruit, ne verront que dans 20 ou 30 ans, quelles que soient nos appartenances politiques. C’est la marque d’un homme d’État exceptionnel : Son Excellence Paul Biya, la force de l’expérience et de l’espoir, qui, en créant le poste de Vice-Président, a une fois de plus eu raison. Ayons le courage et l’honnêteté de reconnaître ce qui est bon pour notre pays. S.E. Paul Biya avait déjà averti ses opposants en 1992 : « Vous ne devez pas jouer avec le Cameroun » (Cameroon Tribune, 12 octobre 1992). En 2026, cet avertissement du chef de l’État demeure pertinent. Son Excellence Paul Biya connaît le Cameroun mieux que chacun d’entre nous. Il montre la voie ; nous devons le soutenir en tout temps et en toutes circonstances. Quiconque prétend aimer le Cameroun davantage que le président Paul Biya est un charlatan. Paul Atanga Nji, ministre de l’Administration territoriale’’ Cet article Création du poste de vice-président au Cameroun : ‘’Toute controverse orchestrée par des acteurs politiques … est vaine’’, Paul Atanga Nji est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

Certains parlent de l’introduction d’un ticket présidentiel dans l’élection présidentielle. Pourquoi le Cameroun devrait-il se préoccuper de ce qui se passe ailleurs ? Le président Paul Biya n’avait-il pas déjà averti que « le Cameroun est… » … « le Cameroun », un pays maître de son propre destin, qui ne suit pas aveuglément les autres sans tenir compte de ses propres réalités ? En ma qualité de ministre de l’Administration territoriale, j’ai eu le privilège de présenter au Sénat et à l’Assemblée nationale, réunis en session conjointe, les amendements au Code électoral relatifs à la création du poste de Vice-Président de la République. J’ai expliqué aux élus de la nation les mérites de l’initiative du chef de l’État. Les membres de l’Assemblée nationale et du Sénat ont adopté les projets de loi du gouvernement à une très large majorité. Conformément aux dispositions légales en vigueur, les textes ont été promulgués par le chef de l’État. Toute controverse orchestrée par des acteurs politiques — principalement ceux de l’opposition — est vaine. Je pense qu’il est temps de mettre fin à la chasse aux sorcières concernant le poste de Vice-Président. La politique de la nation est définie par le chef de l’État. En vertu de ses prérogatives et de son pouvoir discrétionnaire, le chef de l’État nomme des personnes à des fonctions civiles et militaires et peut relever de leurs fonctions les personnes nommées à tout moment. Ces dispositions sont inscrites dans la Constitution et doivent être prises en compte. De plus, Son Excellence Paul Biya connaît le Cameroun mieux que chacun d’entre nous. Je mets quiconque au défi de me prouver le contraire. Dans mon livre, publié avant l’élection présidentielle du 12 octobre 2025 et intitulé « 37 Years of Unwavering Loyalty to the Head of State. Understanding the Meaning of My Ongoing Struggle for Respect for Republican Legality », j’ai souligné que trop d’événements avaient démontré que le chef de l’État avait raison. Il est dans notre intérêt de suivre la voie tracée par Son Excellence Paul Biya, qui a plus de 30 ans d’avance sur nous tous — hauts responsables de la République, hommes politiques, dirigeants de la société civile et autres. Son Excellence Paul Biya possède cette capacité extraordinaire de voir aujourd’hui les obstacles que nous autres, et particulièrement ceux qui font du bruit, ne verront que dans 20 ou 30 ans, quelles que soient nos appartenances politiques. C’est la marque d’un homme d’État exceptionnel : Son Excellence Paul Biya, la force de l’expérience et de l’espoir, qui, en créant le poste de Vice-Président, a une fois de plus eu raison. Ayons le courage et l’honnêteté de reconnaître ce qui est bon pour notre pays. S.E. Paul Biya avait déjà averti ses opposants en 1992 : « Vous ne devez pas jouer avec le Cameroun » (Cameroon Tribune, 12 octobre 1992). En 2026, cet avertissement du chef de l’État demeure pertinent. Son Excellence Paul Biya connaît le Cameroun mieux que chacun d’entre nous. Il montre la voie ; nous devons le soutenir en tout temps et en toutes circonstances. Quiconque prétend aimer le Cameroun davantage que le président Paul Biya est un charlatan. data.title: Sécurité des bâtiments : les maires et les ordres professionnels scellent un partenariat
data.description: © DR Face à la recrudescence des effondrements d'immeubles, les Communes et Villes Unies du Cameroun (CVUC), l'Ordre National des Architectes du Cameroun (ONAC) et l'Ordre National des Ingénieurs de Génie Civil (ONIGC) ont signé ce mercredi 03 septembre 2026 une convention-cadre tripartite historique. Objectif : verrouiller le suivi des chantiers privés après la délivrance du permis de construire. C'est une réponse directe à une crise qui endeuille le Cameroun. Les CVUC, l'ONAC et l'ONIGC ont décidé de siffler la fin du désordre dans le secteur du BTP. Réunies le 03 septembre, les trois parties ont paraphé une convention qui change la donne. Fini le permis de construire délivré puis oublié. Désormais, le dispositif impose une maîtrise d'œuvre conjointe associant obligatoirement architecte et ingénieur sur les chantiers privés. Le texte prévoit des garde-fous concrets : instauration d'un carnet de suivi de chantier, obligation de points d'arrêt aux étapes critiques des travaux pour validation, et mécanisme de paiement progressif des honoraires des professionnels pour éviter les abandons. L'ambition politique est claire : prévenir les malfaçons, stopper les modifications anarchiques des plans approuvés et surtout, redonner aux mairies leur pouvoir de contrôle administratif, souvent contourné. Pour ne pas brusquer le système, une phase pilote sera lancée dans des communes volontaires, avec deux innovations majeures : la digitalisation du carnet de suivi et la formation des agents municipaux. À travers cet accord, les collectivités et les ordres professionnels envoient un message fort : la sécurité des populations prime sur les économies de bout de chandelle. Cet article Sécurité des bâtiments : les maires et les ordres professionnels scellent un partenariat est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun/ Fiscalité : mise en demeure des hautes personnalités et fonctionnaires
data.description: © DR Dans un communiqué signé le 02 septembre 2026, le Ministre des Finances annonce la fin du délai de déclaration de l'IRPP et de la TPF pour l'exercice 2025. Les retardataires, notamment les hautes personnalités et les salariés du public et parapublic, ont sept jours pour se régulariser sous peine de sanctions lourdes, dont la publication de leurs noms dans la presse. Le ton se durcit à la Direction Générale des Impôts. Dans un communiqué signé le 02 septembre 2026, le Ministre Louis Paul Motaze rappelle que les délais de souscription de la déclaration annuelle de l'Impôt sur le Revenu des Personnes Physiques (IRPP) et de la Taxe sur la Propriété Foncière (TPF) sont arrivés à échéance. Initialement fixés au 31 juillet 2026 puis prorogés au 30 août 2026, ces délais concernaient spécifiquement les contribuables non professionnels de la catégorie des hautes personnalités et les salariés des secteurs public et parapublic. Si le Ministre félicite ceux qui se sont acquittés de leurs obligations, il lance un ultimatum aux retardataires. À compter de la publication du communiqué, qui vaut mise en demeure, ils disposent d'un délai de sept jours pour régulariser leur situation conformément à l'article L 3 du Livre des Procédures Fiscales. Passé ce délai, l'administration fiscale promet une tolérance zéro. Elle brandit la taxation d'office avec majorations, une amende forfaitaire de 100 000 FCFA prévue à l'article L 99, et surtout, l'arme politique : la publication de la liste des défaillants par voie de presse en application de l'article L3 bis du Code Général des Impôts. Une mesure de "name and shame" qui vise directement l'élite administrative camerounaise. Cet article Cameroun/ Fiscalité : mise en demeure des hautes personnalités et fonctionnaires est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : les enseignants du supérieur décident de paralyser la rentrée académique
data.description: © DR Un mot d'ordre de grève du Syndicat national des enseignants du supérieur place ces derniers en position de grève depuis le 03 septembre dernier et ce jusqu'à satisfaction de leurs revendications. Une fois de plus, le Bureau national du Syndicat des enseignants du supérieur met les activités académiques au point mort. Le Synes, au terme d'une réunion extraordinaire de son bureau exécutif en fin de semaine dernière, a lancé le débrayage dans les 11 universités publiques. Le mot d'ordre demande d'imposer « une rentrée académique morte » à travers une grève illimitée. L'entrée en grève au supérieur se base sur trois points de revendications faisant monter la colère. Les enseignants attendent une suite à la demande d'audience adressée au président de la République en date du 20 janvier 2025 ; le paiement intégral des sommes dues de l'allocation spéciale pour la modernisation de la recherche, à tous les enseignants sans exclusive ainsi que l'apurement total de la dette académique. Parmi les points d'achoppement dans la relation entre enseignants et gouvernement, le syndicat évoque aussi « l'indifférence persistante de du gouvernement de la République en ce qui concerne ses engagements en matière de dialogue social, de la gouvernance universitaire et de la préservation d'un climat social et apaisé au sein de nos universités publiques ». Le Synes dénonce par ailleurs le silence et le mépris affiché par les autorités publiques. Toutes choses qui démontrent du désengagement des enseignants et de la dégradation progressive des relations avec les autorités. D'après les confidences du Bureau du syndicat à des médias, le gouvernement a amorcé le paiement de la dette académique en promettant de payer l'intégralité sur trois ans à compter de 2024. Mais, seules trois universités ont reçu leurs paiements. L'enveloppe encore due est d'environ 15 milliards 600 millions de francs CFA. Alors que le paiement est attendu, les questions qui se posent sont de l'effectivité de la grève dans tous les campus universitaires publics et de la durée de la grève. Ces dernières années, certaines annonces de grèves n'ont pas abouti au débrayage. D'autres, ont débouché sur la suspension des activités académiques. Mais ces grèves n'ont pas persisté jusqu'à satisfaction des revendications. Une fois que le gouvernement commence à régler des allocations spéciales pour la modernisation de la recherche, le mouvement s'arrête. Cet article Cameroun : les enseignants du supérieur décident de paralyser la rentrée académique est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
